transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

I'm just really struggling with how my face looks, especially my nose. It feels completely crooked and deformed, and it's ruining my entire appearance. I just can't stop thinking about how awful it looks to everyone else.
Do you find yourself spending a lot of time checking your nose in mirrors, trying to hide or camouflage it, or asking others for reassurance about how it looks?

Yes, I'm constantly checking my nose in every single mirror or window I pass, and I try to hide it by using heavy contouring makeup or holding my hand over my face. I also ask my family if it looks okay all the time, but even when they reassure me, I just can't bring myself to believe them.
How sure are you that your nose is actually deformed? Do you feel 100% certain about it, or is there a part of you that thinks it might actually look okay?

I am 100% certain that my nose is deformed and completely crooked. To me, the flaw is incredibly obvious and ruins my whole face, even though everyone else keeps telling me it looks completely normal. I just can't see it any other way.
Do you experience repetitive, unwanted thoughts or feel driven to perform rituals about things unrelated to your appearance, such as cleanliness, safety, or order?
No, I don't experience anything like that with cleanliness, safety, or order. All of my worries and repetitive habits are completely focused on my appearance and how deformed my face looks.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were ['Body Dysmorphic Disorder', 'Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder']. Based on the patient's report, they do not have obsessive thoughts or compulsive rituals unrelated to their appearance (such as cleanliness, safety, or order). This rules out Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder. The patient's symptoms perfectly align with Body Dysmorphic Disorder, characterized by preoccupation with a perceived defect in appearance, repetitive behaviors (mirror checking, camouflaging, reassurance seeking), and delusional intensity beliefs (100% conviction). Thus, the diagnosis is finalized as Body Dysmorphic Disorder.

inference_history.note: The patient presents with intense distress and preoccupation regarding a perceived physical defect (their nose), which they describe as crooked and deformed. This presentation is highly characteristic of Body Dysmorphic Disorder (BDD). We also include Obsessive-Compulsive Disorder (due to obsessive thoughts), Delusional Disorder (if the belief is held with delusional conviction), and Major Depressive Disorder (which can co-occur or present with severe negative self-evaluation) in the initial differential diagnosis.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits a severe, distressing preoccupation with a perceived physical defect (a crooked nose) that is unnoticeable to others. This preoccupation is accompanied by repetitive behaviors, including mirror checking, camouflaging, and reassurance-seeking. The patient has a delusional level of conviction about the defect, and denies general obsessive-compulsive symptoms unrelated to appearance.
